name: Congenital Myasthenic Syndrome Due to Defective Synthesis or Recycling of Acetylcholine

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Myasthenic Syndromes

criteria.description: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness with onset in infancy or early childhood
Electrophysiological evidence of impaired neuromuscular transmission (e.g., decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation)
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in acetylcholine synthesis or recycling (e.g., CHAT, SLC5A7)
Improvement of symptoms with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors or other targeted therapies
Exclusion of autoimmune myasthenia gravis and other neuromuscular disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness with electrophysiological evidence of neuromuscular transmission defect plus identification of pathogenic variants in relevant genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is critical for definitive diagnosis; electrophysiological studies support clinical findings.

searchTerms: muscle weakness that worsens with use
drooping eyelid that worsens with tiredness
partial eye muscle weakness with changing severity

common.symptomName: Bulbar muscle weakness causing dysarthria and dysphagia
searchTerms: weak throat muscles causing speech and swallowing issues
bulbar weakness with dysarthria and dysphagia
difficulty speaking and swallowing from muscle weakness

common.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness leading to episodic respiratory insufficiency
searchTerms: weak breathing muscles causing breathing problems
episodes of respiratory failure from muscle weakness
respiratory insufficiency due to weak muscles
problems with automatic body functions like sweating
abnormal sweating and other autonomic symptoms

laboratory: Normal autoimmune antibody panels (e.g., anti-AChR antibodies negative)
imaging: Possible mild muscle atrophy on muscle MRI in chronic cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in CHAT gene (choline acetyltransferase)
Pathogenic variants in SLC5A7 gene (choline transporter)
Other presynaptic gene mutations affecting acetylcholine synthesis or recycling
other: Electrophysiological studies showing decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation

distinguishingFeatures: Associated with malignancy (e.g., small cell lung cancer)
Facilitation of muscle strength with exercise
Antibodies against presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels
Mutations in postsynaptic or synaptic basal lamina genes

redFlags: Progressive respiratory failure requiring ventilatory support
Rapid onset of severe bulbar weakness
Poor or paradoxical response to acetylcholinesterase inhibitors
references: Engel AG, Shen XM, Selcen D, Sine SM. Congenital myasthenic syndromes: pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment. Lancet Neurol. 2015;14(4):420-434.
